correctness.rationale: For each m>=2 the strong Markov property at the first repeat leaves m-t+1 unseen symbols, giving the asserted independent geometric waiting-time law; the m+1 endpoint has completed coverage at time m. Coupling conditional laws at consecutive t cancels all common geometric stages, leaving an almost-sure nonnegative difference and strict inequality with positive probability. Conditional stochastic monotonicity plus an independent-copy covariance identity proves negative quadrant dependence and strictly negative covariance. The birthday survival product converges with all fixed moments to Rayleigh by Gaussian tails; the exact harmonic decrement g_m(b)=m H_m+1-D_m(b)-1_{b=m+1}, its quadratic expansion, and exponential control of large b give normalized covariance -sqrt(pi/8). The independent geometric coverage-stage variance is m^2 H_m^(2)-m H_m and the Rayleigh variance gives the stated exact correlation constant. The actual standalone verifier passed 3,493 exact-rational and numerical assertions; finite checks are not used as infinite proofs.

originality.rationale: Exact prior-work queries were run in the mathematical research index and publicly accessible literature, and accessible prior mathematical claims were screened for overlap. The primary Myers-Wilf preprint treats independent coupon collectors, repeated collections and final singleton counts, not the same-stream birthday/completion conditional law. Flajolet-Sedgewick treats birthday and coverage stopping times as marginal classical problems; the located passages do not give their conditional stochastic-order theorem or mixed covariance asymptotics. Related indexed results concern reset collection, hash collision envelopes or next-step species discoveries. This supports best-knowledge originality of the joint reverse-regression and sharp mixed moment statement; neither search failures nor partition membership are used to assert uniqueness.
residual_risks: The large classic Analytic Combinatorics text was not exhaustively inspected; an unlocated joint-statistic remark or later appendix could exist.

value.rationale: The two canonically motivated stopping times from one iid occupancy stream display a surprising finite-sample inverse relationship despite describing progress through the same draw sequence. A strict stochastic monotonicity theorem yields all increasing-transform covariance inequalities and negative quadrant dependence, not merely a particular elementary identity. An exact finite covariance algorithm and the sharp universal Rayleigh covariance constant/correlation decay quantify the effect. The mathematical contribution is the complete dependence structure and rate, not an arbitrary parameter slice or a recomputation of classical stopping-time marginals.
